overall: Early morning conditions in Los Angeles show a persistent marine layer with patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies, holding overnight lows in the low-to-mid 60s. The running max of 64.9°F was established near midnight and temperatures have been essentially flat-to-slightly-cooling through dawn, consistent with a strong onshore marine influence. Daytime heating is yet to begin and will depend on how quickly the fog/cloud deck breaks — a typical July marine layer pattern for coastal LA.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate spread with GFS the outlier at 74.6°F; ECMWF (73.0°F) and HRRR (72.5°F) cluster closely near the NWS forecast of 'near 73°F,' while NBM (69.5°F) is the cool outlier likely reflecting cloud-cover suppression. The META model — the most reliable fused signal — assigns 80% probability to the 72–73°F even bucket, indicating strong convergence around the low-70s despite GFS running warmer.
max_temp_prediction: Peak heating is expected around 14–16h ET once the marine layer partially breaks; with fog and cloud cover persisting into the late morning, some suppression of afternoon highs is likely relative to the GFS outlier. The NWS forecast of 73°F, ECMWF/HRRR clustering at 72.5–73°F, and the META model's 80% concentration on 72–73°F all point to a final daily high near 72–73°F. For the active ODD-bucket Kalshi market, the top bucket is 71–72°F at 35.6%, which covers ~71.0–72.9°F — this is the most probable single bucket, though a reading of 72.5–73°F landing in the 73–74°F odd bucket is a real secondary risk if cloud clearing is faster than expected; confidence is moderate-to-good.
